behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak

Stage 3 consumes the SIDs; it does not write back into them. The only data-dependent quantity updated during training, π^ℓ_k, is an EMA over train-batch assignments only.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: γ = 0 at every level, so the cost is the pure Poincaré distance; gyro residual and gyro-sum reconstruction unchanged; π table still built and the switches still compiled in, but the run is not trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the single trained arm — gyro residual, gyro-sum reconstruction, Poincaré cost times (1 − a_ik), K = 256/512/512.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: replace gyro-subtraction with tangent subtraction r^ℓ = log_0(r^{ℓ−1}) − log_0(c_ℓ), the gyro-sum reconstruction with exp_0(Σ log_0 c_ℓ), and d_P with the Euclidean distance ‖·‖; the affinity factor (1 − a_ik) is retained exactly as in the both-on arm; not trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training sequences only, count ordered adjacent pairs (u → v). Weight each pair w_{u→v} = n_{u→v} / pop_v^{0.5} (the square-root popularity correction already used in the frozen recipe). Bin every successor v into one of 256 clusters produced once by k-means on the frozen training text embeddings. Set π_u[m] = Σ_{v→m} w_{u→v} / Σ_v w_{u→v}, an L1-normalised 256-vector; items with no outgoing train transition receive π̄. Computed once before epoch 1, stored as a constant table, never recomputed from validation or test data.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions, aggregated into a per-item successor profile over a frozen 256-bin item partition.
ideas.cost_estimate: Baseline 0.145–0.16 s per epoch on four GPUs. The added work per step is one Möbius addition/subtraction over the batch (O(B·d)), one 4096×256 by 256×512 affinity matmul (~0.54 GFLOP, sub-millisecond), and doubled distance matrices at levels 2 and 3. Measured estimate: +10–15% of the quantizer stage, i.e. 0.165–0.18 s per epoch, ~4.0–4.3 s per 24-step epoch pass total; 3000 epochs ≈ 8.5–9.0 minutes against the baseline's ~7.5–8.0 minutes. Extra trainable parameters: 2·512·d ≈ 65k at d = 64, negligible against the frozen budget. The 24556×256 behaviour-profile table is a fixed 25 MB buffer, not a parameter. Stage 3 protocol, sequence length and vocabulary usage are untouched apart from K2 = K3 = 512.
ideas.coupling_equation: k^ℓ_i = argmin_k [ d_P( r^{ℓ−1}_i , c_{ℓk} ) · (1 − γ · a^ℓ_{ik}) ], with r^ℓ_i = r^{ℓ−1}_i ⊖ c_{ℓ,k^ℓ_i}, γ = 1.
ideas.coupling_path: encoder → v_i → gyro residual r^{ℓ−1} → cost d_P(r^{ℓ−1}, c_{ℓk})·(1 − a_{ik}) → argmin gives k^ℓ → next gyro residual → token string (k¹,k²,k³) → frozen Stage 3 → test_recall@10. The behaviour profile enters only through the multiplier on the curved distance, and the curve enters only through the residual algebra and the same distance, so deleting either changes k^ℓ and therefore the SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the third token is being wasted because the flat-approximated residual collapses, then (a) the gyro residual keeps ‖r^3‖ at a curvature-determined scale instead of near zero, and (b) the affinity term splits each L2 cell's ~20 items into behaviourally coherent sub-groups, so the L3 code becomes a behaviour discriminator that Stage 3 can predict from the prefix and context. Worth keeping only if distinct L3 triples rise from 1298 to at least 3000, mean L3 codes per L2 cell rises from 1.04 to at least 2.5, mean affinity a_{i,k*} of assigned items exceeds 0.3, and d_P reconstruction stays within 5% of the baseline value while test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer recursion (residual and reconstruction) and inside the level-2 and level-3 assignment cost, during Stage-2 training.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Möbius gyro-addition and gyro-subtraction in the Poincaré ball plus the Poincaré distance, at fixed negative curvature c = 1, used both as the residual algebra and as the assignment metric.
ideas.key_change: Replace the RQ residual subtraction with Poincaré gyro-subtraction and the reconstruction with the Möbius gyro-sum of the chosen codewords, and at levels 2 and 3 multiply each Poincaré distance by (1 − a_ik) before the argmin, with 512 codewords at those levels.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, the popularity correction, the k-means partition and the π table are built exclusively from the Stage-2 train split, before any training step, and are frozen for the whole run. No validation or test sequence, no future-relative-to-split item, and no Stage-3 interaction ever enters π_i, π^ℓ_k, the codewords or the SID strings. Stage 3 consumes the SIDs; it does not write back into them. The only data-dependent quantity updated during training, π^ℓ_k, is an EMA over train-batch assignments only.
ideas.motivation: The measured failure across rounds one and two is depth collapse, not codeword shortage: 24556 training items give 1251 distinct L2 pairs (19.6 items per cell) but only 1298 distinct L3 triples — about 1.04 L3 codes per L2 cell, so the third token carries almost no information. Round one, which kept 1.76 L3 codes per cell, scored 0.0544 against round two's 0.0517. The cause is structural: the third-level tangent residual r^3 = r^2 − log_0(c_2) is near zero for most items, so the ball degenerates to flat space exactly where the finest partition is needed. Every mechanism so far tried to fix depth by moving items (toward a behaviour hub, along a geodesic step) and every one of them merged prefixes.
ideas.novelty: Two pieces that are absent from the tried set (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID). (i) The residual algebra is changed from tangent subtraction to Poincaré gyro-subtraction, with the decoder defined as the Möbius gyro-sum, so the greedy residual is exact by gyro-cancellation and no gain constant is introduced. (ii) The deep-level assignment cost is the Poincaré distance multiplied per (item, codeword) by (1 − a_ik), a train-only successor-profile affinity, so behaviour chooses which of 512 deep codes an item receives. Prior mechanisms moved codebook positions, set per-level curvature, ranked items radially, or applied cones/boosts; none changes the residual algebra, and none makes the distance non-monotone per pair so that behaviour can actually flip the argmin and therefore the token.
ideas.observables: distinct L3 triples (baseline 1298, target ≥3000); mean distinct L3 codes per L2 cell (1.04 → ≥2.5); mean behaviour purity a_{i,k*} of assigned items (baseline undefined/0 → >0.3); mean and 90th-percentile ‖r^3‖ (should stop collapsing toward zero); reconstruction d_P (must stay within 5%); L2 distinct pairs; Stage-3 third-token prefix hit rate; test_recall@10, recall@5, ndcg@10.

risks: The affinity term pulls codes away from reconstruction-optimal choices and can trade semantic fidelity for partition (this is why the 5% reconstruction guard is recorded). 512 codes at level 2 may shatter the L1 hierarchy into noise. Möbius subtraction of two nearly aligned points at large radius can inflate ‖r‖ toward the boundary and route many items onto a few extreme codes, re-creating collapse in a different form. The 256-bin successor profile (≈96 items per bin) is smooth, so a_ik may be too weak to flip many argmins; if purity stays near zero the affinity is inert. A finer third token is harder for Stage 3 to generate, so prefix counts can rise while test_recall@10 falls — that is the outcome to record, not to hide.
ideas.safeguards: clip ‖x‖ to 1 − 1e-7 inside every tanh and every denominator; compute d_P through the arcosh form with the argument clamped to ≥ 1 + 1e-12; after each gyro-subtraction renormalise r^ℓ to ‖r^ℓ‖ ≤ 1 − 1e-6 keeping its direction; clamp C^ℓ_{ik} ≥ 0; floor ε at 1e-3 and detach it; L2-normalise π_i and π^ℓ_k and substitute π̄ when a codeword's EMA mass is zero; keep the frozen gradient clip and learning rate unchanged; log mean/p90 ‖r^ℓ‖ every epoch and halt-and-report if ‖r^3‖ grows beyond 1 − 1e-3 for more than 1% of items (boundary saturation); log reconstruction d_P every epoch against the 5% guard. Origin-collapse check required by the contract: the objective's minimum is not at the ball's origin because the gyro-sum reconstruction target is v_i itself and the affinity multiplier is bounded below by 0, so both act against radial contraction; the mean ‖v_i‖ and mean ‖r^ℓ‖ are logged to confirm no degeneration to one or two prefixes per level.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs — frozen text embeddings e_i for the 24556 training items, the frozen 256-bin successor profile table π (24556×256), codeword tables c_1 ∈ R^{256×d}, c_2, c_3 ∈ R^{512×d}, the frozen optimiser and β_com. Outputs — the SID triple (k¹_i, k²_i, k³_i) for every item, the EMA codeword profiles π^ℓ, and the scalar losses and reconstruction diagnostics logged per epoch.

specification.text: Fixed curvature c = 1 (curvature is a gauge; the encoder's tanh scaling absorbs the scale, so no curvature value is chosen or swept). Ball B = {v ∈ R^d : ‖v‖ < 1}. Möbius addition x ⊕ y = ((1 + 2⟨x,y⟩ + ‖y‖²)x + (1 − ‖x‖²)y) / (1 + 2⟨x,y⟩ + ‖x‖²‖y‖²); gyro-subtraction x ⊖ y = x ⊕ (−y). Poincaré distance d_P(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2‖x−y‖² / ((1−‖x‖²)(1−‖y‖²))). Encoder emits t_i ∈ R^d, v_i = tanh(‖t_i‖/2) · t_i/‖t_i‖. RQ recursion: r^0_i = v_i; for ℓ = 1,2,3, k^ℓ_i = argmin_k [ d_P(r^{ℓ−1}_i, c_{ℓk}) · (1 − γ a^ℓ_{ik}) ] with γ = 1, then r^ℓ_i = r^{ℓ−1}_i ⊖ c_{ℓ,k^ℓ_i}. Reconstruction ẑ_i = c_{1,k¹} ⊕ c_{2,k²} ⊕ c_{3,k³}; loss L = d_P(v_i, ẑ_i)² + β_com·Σ_ℓ ‖log_0(r^ℓ_i)‖² (β_com inherited unchanged from the frozen recipe). Level 1 uses γ_1 = 0 so the coarse semantic hierarchy stays purely geometric; the coupling is confined to levels 2 and 3. a^ℓ_{ik} = max(0, cos(π_i − π̄, π^ℓ_k − π̄)), with π_i a fixed 256-bin successor profile, π̄ its mean, and π^ℓ_k an EMA (decay 0.99) of π_i over items currently assigned to codeword k at level ℓ, stop-gradient. Soft assignment for the straight-through gradient uses softmax(−C^ℓ_{ik}/ε) with ε = median_{i,k} C^ℓ_{ik} over the batch, detached.

ideas.title: Möbius-gyro residual RQ with behaviour-affinity-weighted Poincaré deep assignment (K = 256/512/512)

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: S^_i is set to zero for every item, so a_i = x_i and the L3 token is decided purely by curvature against residual geometry; this run would show whether the behaviour direction, not the extra 256 codes, is what fills the new tokens.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled run above: behaviour address, Lorentz midpoint, Klein power diagram, 512 L3 codes, standard RQ-VAE loss. Only this arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: exp_0, the Lorentz midpoint and the Klein power diagram are replaced by the identity, the arithmetic mean (x_i+b_i)/2 and Euclidean argmin ||a_i - e_k/R||^2, keeping 512 L3 codes and the same behaviour term; this run would show whether the 1/(1-||K||^2) margin weighting, i.e. the curvature, is what converts behaviour contrast into a usable partition.
ideas.behavior_computation: Directed adjacent item-item transition counts A_ij from TRAIN sequences only (before any Stage3 run), row-normalised, mean-centred by the global successor marginal pi, factorised by truncated SVD on the train matrix, projected by a fixed seed-0 Gaussian map and scaled by the measured median norm R_b. Items with zero train out-transitions get S^_i = 0 and fall back to the content address.
ideas.behavior_signal: Successor-contrast signature of each item: its train transition row minus the global train successor marginal, truncated to its dominant spectral directions and L2-normalised, then linearly embedded in the SID latent space; plus its norm-matched Poincare image.
ideas.cost_estimate: offline (transition counts, rank-90% SVD, behaviour cache) ~10 s once. Per step at 1024 items/card: score matmul 1024x512x64 = 33.5M MAC (~0.07 GFLOP) plus ~1.3 MFLOP for exp/log/Klein/midpoint, i.e. <1% of a 6.0-6.7 ms step; per epoch 0.150 -> ~0.151 s, 3000 epochs ~450 -> ~452 s on four cards. Extra memory: 24556x64 behaviour cache (~6 MB) and 256x64 extra codewords. Stage3 adds 256 output-embedding rows at position 3 only.
ideas.coupling_equation: a_i = Mid_Lorentz(exp_0^1(r_i^(3)/R), exp_0^1(P S^_i / R_b)); k_i = argmax_k (1-||K(q_k)||^2)^(-1/2) (<K(a_i), K(q_k)> - 1), where P S^_i is the centred successor-contrast behaviour term and the exp/Klein/gamma factors are the curved term, so a behaviour offset flips a token only through the curvature-weighted margin gamma_k(1-||K||^2).
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour signature -> Poincare behaviour point -> Lorentz geodesic midpoint with the level-3 content residual point -> Klein power-diagram score against the level-3 codebook -> argmax -> third SID token -> straight-through commitment/reconstruction gradient -> encoder residuals -> all three prefixes. Removing behaviour sets the address to the content point; removing curvature replaces the midpoint and the score by their Euclidean counterparts; either changes which tokens exist.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The behaviour-resolved L3 address makes the third token informative, so distinct L3 prefixes rise well above 2201 (target >= 4000, mean L3 codes per L2 pair >= 2) with all 512 L3 codes occupied, within-prefix train successor entropy falls, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 while recall@5 and ndcg@10 rise with it. It is worth keeping if the rise in distinct triples and the behaviour-induced L3 flip fraction coexist with the recall gain; if triples do not rise, the mechanism is falsified by its own observable.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the level-3 quantization/assignment step of the RQ-VAE during Stage 2 training: it decides the third SID token of every item on every step, and through the unchanged commitment and reconstruction losses it also re-shapes the encoder that produces all three residuals.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Negative curvature c = 1: Poincare exponential map exp_0^1, the exact Lorentz-model geodesic midpoint (normalised Minkowski sum of hyperboloid lifts), the Klein projection K(a) = 2a/(1+||a||^2), and the Klein power-diagram score gamma_k(<K(a),K(q_k)> - 1), which equals -gamma_a * cosh(sqrt(c) d_c(a,q_k)) and is therefore exact hyperbolic nearest-codeword.
ideas.key_change: At RQ level 3 only, the code index is chosen for a geodesic midpoint of the content residual point and a per-item behaviour point in the unit Poincare ball, against 512 codewords, by exact hyperbolic nearest-codeword; the RQ-VAE loss is unchanged, so the encoder is reshaped through the ordinary straight-through/commitment path and the token itself carries the behaviour.
ideas.leakage_boundary: A_ij, pi, the SVD basis, the projection, R and R_b are all computed from the training split only and frozen before Stage 2; validation/test items and their interactions never enter the count matrix, the basis, the reference medians or the SID assignment; Stage 3 keeps its frozen protocol and only consumes the resulting SIDs.
ideas.motivation: Round two moved every item toward a popularity-adjusted behaviour hub; prefix capacity fell to 230/1251/1298 and test_recall@10 fell to 0.0517. Round one kept 2201 L3 prefixes and reached 0.0544. The one consistent signal across both negatives is that recall tracks deep-prefix capacity. In the frozen 3-level 256-code quantizer there are 1769 distinct L2 pairs but only 2201 distinct L3 triples at 24556 items, i.e. 1.24 L3 codes per L2 pair: the third token is almost a deterministic function of the second, so the ~13.9 items sharing each L2 pair are behaviourally indistinguishable to the recommender. The deepest level is the cheapest place to buy behaviour-resolvable capacity, and no earlier round put behaviour there without also moving the points.
ideas.novelty: (i) Geometry acts on the ADDRESS used for the code decision and on the decision boundary, never on the item positions: r_i is untouched, so the mechanism cannot merge cells by displacement as round two did. (ii) The behaviour object is a CENTRED successor-contrast direction (train transition row minus the global successor marginal, then SVD-truncated and L2-normalised), which structurally deletes the popularity/hub component that destroyed round two; contrast, not co-consumption mass. (iii) The curved operations are an exact Lorentz geodesic midpoint and the Klein power diagram (hyperbolic Voronoi), not a Frechet codebook update, not Sinkhorn, not a curvature-per-level controller, not successor-profile smoothing, not a cone, not a radial rank. (iv) L3 codewords go 256 -> 512, but the extra 256 codes are only usable because behaviour supplies a direction; capacity alone would just duplicate near-identical residuals.
ideas.observables: distinct L1/L2/L3 prefixes (expect L3 >= 4000), mean distinct L3 per L2 pair (expect >= 2), L3 code occupancy over 512 (expect no dead codes, lower Gini), within-prefix train successor entropy (expect lower at L3), L3 geodesic reconstruction error (expect a small rise), median address radius versus median content radius (curvature liveness), end-of-training behaviour flip fraction (fraction of items whose L3 token changes when S^_i is zeroed in a single diagnostic forward pass; expect >= 20%), and Stage3 test_recall@10 / recall@5 / ndcg@10.
risks: The Lorentz midpoint contracts radii, which can push addresses toward the centre where curvature is weak and make geometry-off and both-on nearly identical (median address radius must be reported). The commitment/codebook terms may drag e_k back onto r_i and erase behaviour control at equilibrium (measured by the flip fraction). A 512-token level-3 vocabulary may be harder for Stage3 to learn. Centring does not fully remove blockbusters from the contrast signature. Klein cells are unbalanced, so some of the 512 codes may own almost no items. L3 reconstruction error will rise slightly.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||r_i^(3)/R|| and ||h_i/R_b|| to 3.0 so the ball point stays at radius <= 0.905; floor the Minkowski norm at 1e-8 and fall back to a_i = x_i if it is violated; clamp ||a_i|| <= 1-1e-3; floor (1-||K(q_k)||^2) at 1e-8; zero-transition items get S^_i = 0 so their token is pure content; the address transform is a deterministic re-parameterisation and not an objective, so its minimum is not at the ball origin and the encoder cannot collapse toward the origin through it (the standard reconstruction term remains the only attractor); report median address radius, L3 occupancy and the behaviour flip fraction every 500 epochs as diagnostics only, with no early stopping and no arm switched off during the run.
ideas.spec_equations: L(x) = ((1+||x||^2)/(1-||x||^2), 2x/(1-||x||^2)); <u,v>_M = -u_0 v_0 + u.v; m = (L(x)+L(y))/sqrt(max(-<L(x)+L(y),L(x)+L(y)>_M, 1e-8)); a = m_{1:}/(1+m_0); clamp ||a|| <= 1-1e-3; K(a) = 2a/(1+||a||^2); gamma_k = (1-||K(q_k)||^2)^(-1/2); S_ik = gamma_k(<K(a_i),K(q_k)>-1); k_i = argmax_k S_ik; check cosh(sqrt(c) d_c(a,q_k)) = -gamma_a S_ik, so the rule is exact.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the level-3 residual r_i^(3), the cached behaviour signature S^_i, the level-3 codebook e_k (k = 1..512) and the two measured medians R and R_b. Outputs are the level-3 code index k_i for every train item (the third SID token), the midpoint address a_i (diagnostic), and the unchanged RQ-VAE loss.

specification.text:
c = 1 (curvature -1, fixed); d = frozen RQ-VAE latent width.
OFFLINE (train split, once): A_ij = adjacent (i->j) counts over train sequences; T_i = A_i/max(1,sum_j A_ij); pi = (sum_i A_i)/sum_ij A_ij; A~_i = T_i - pi; SVD A~ = U S V^T, keep m = smallest rank with cumulative squared singular energy >= 0.90 (reported), S_i = U_i S; S^_i = S_i/||S_i|| (0 if ||S_i|| < 1e-8). Fixed P in R^{d x m}, seed 0, N(0,1)/sqrt(m); h_i = P S^_i; R_b = median_i ||h_i||. Cache b_i = tanh(||h_i||/(2 R_b)) * h^_i for all 24556 train items (fixed buffer, no gradient).
APERTURE (once, after encoder init, train items only): R = median_i ||r_i^(3)||, r_i^(3) = z_i - e_{k1} - e_{k2}.
PER STEP, batch B: x_i = exp_0^1(r_i^(3)/R) = tanh(||r_i||/(2R)) r^_i with ||r_i||/R clamped to 3.0; a_i = Mid_L(x_i, b_i); q_k = exp_0^1(e_k/R), k = 1..512 at L3 only (L1, L2 stay 256); K(a) = 2a/(1+||a||^2); gamma_k = (1-||K(q_k)||^2)^(-1/2); k_i = argmax_k gamma_k (<K(a_i),K(q_k)> - 1); quantized L3 vector = e_{k_i} straight-through; loss unchanged.

ideas.title: Successor-contrast Lorentz geodesic midpoint address with a 512-code curved L3 assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Same four-level architecture, same Poincare operator, same impostor pairs and margin, but c_ij set to 1 for every pair, so the push becomes behaviour-blind and acts like a plain curved diversity hinge. Implemented as a single flag that overwrites the contrast matrix with ones; wired but not trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full run described here: four 256-codeword levels, contrast-weighted Poincare hinge on the quantised code vectors, margin from the initial median geodesic distance, lambda from the initial loss ratio.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Same four-level architecture, same contrast weights c_ij and same margin (recomputed as the median initial Euclidean distance so the scale matches), but d_P replaced by the Euclidean distance between the same quantised vectors and the exp map replaced by the identity. Implemented as one flag swapping the metric call; wired but not trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the TRAINING split sequences only, over 24556 items: A_ij = count of consecutive pairs (item_t = i, item_{t+1} = j); p_i = (A_i. + 1)/(sum_j A_ij + V) with V = 24556 (add-one, no tuned smoothing); c_ij = 1 - cos(p_i, p_j) clipped to [0,1]; items with no outgoing transition get c = 0 and are excluded from P. The impostor list is materialised once before Stage 2 and frozen for the whole run.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transition contrast, i.e. the dissimilarity of two items' row-normalised successor distributions, used with a reversed (repulsive) sign.
ideas.cost_estimate: +8192 parameters (one extra 256 x 32 codebook). Per step: at most 4096 x 4 = 16384 Poincare distance evaluations, roughly 0.1-0.4 ms on top of the ~6.3 ms step (24 steps/epoch, 0.15 s/epoch), so about +3-8 percent, i.e. 0.155-0.17 s/epoch and still ~8 minutes for 3000 epochs plus one ~1 minute GPU precompute of the impostor lists. Stage 3 pays one extra token per item.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_push = (1/|B_P|) * sum_{(i,j) in B_P, pi2(i)=pi2(j)} c_ij * [ m - (2/sqrt(c)) artanh( sqrt(c) || (-q_i) (+)_c q_j || ) ]_+^2 , with q_i = exp_0^c( sum_{l=1..4} e_{l,k_l(i)} ).
ideas.coupling_path: Behaviour contrast c_ij selects and weights the pair; only that pair's quantised code vectors are compared under d_P; the gradient of that single term updates e_{3,k} and e_{4,k} directly, which changes the residual assignment of the next step and therefore the emitted tokens. Removing c_ij removes the per-pair variation of the force; replacing d_P by Euclidean distance removes the radial grading; either change alters the same scalar that produces the codebook gradient, so it is one pathway and not two losses added together.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If separation created by behaviour contrast is what the recall metric was reading (behaviour-contrast rho = +0.7104 in the 107-pair table) and prefix capacity was the binding constraint, then distinct L3 prefixes must rise above the 1298/2201 range, L4 must not collapse to a handful of codes, and Stage3 test_recall@10 must exceed 0.065. Observed through: distinct prefix counts per level, mean Poincare radius, L4 codebook perplexity, and test_recall@10 from the single frozen run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the RQ-VAE training loss at the deepest quantisation levels (all four codebooks through the straight-through path, with the parent mask fixed at level two), and consequently in the geometric layout of the level-3 and level-4 codebooks.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (ball radius 1) Poincare ball; exp_0^c tangent-to-ball map for the quantised vector and Poincare geodesic distance d_P with Mobius addition. Curvature is deliberately not trained and not per-cell, because curvature is a gauge; the only geometric content used is the metric's radial distortion, which makes the same hinge push much harder near the boundary than near the origin.
ideas.key_change: Take the behaviourally most-contrasting text-nearest neighbours of each item inside the same level-2 prefix and push their quantised code vectors apart along the Poincare metric, with a hinge that switches off as soon as the pair is separated by the median initial geodesic distance; simultaneously widen the SID to four levels of 256 codewords so the newly created separation can be committed to tokens.
ideas.leakage_boundary: A_ij is built only from training-split sequences; the text embedding used for text-kNN is item metadata that is not fitted on any validation or test interaction; the margin m is a median over the same frozen training pair list. No validation or test user, sequence, transition or metric ever enters the pair construction, the margin, or the codebook.
ideas.motivation: Both negative rounds lost recall by MERGING deep prefixes (round two kept 1298 L3 prefixes at 0.05165, round one kept 2201 at 0.05439). The behaviour signal has so far only been used as an attractive force (move points toward a successor hub), which is exactly the operation that destroys depth. Separately, text-nearest items that are behaviourally unrelated keep sharing a prefix, and the 3x256 quantiser has no room left at level three. This idea reverses the sign of the behaviour force and adds the one architectural change the brief declares legal (a fourth level), so the partition can only become finer at depth.
ideas.novelty: Not attraction to a popularity-adjusted successor barycentre (round two), not successor-weighted Frechet codebook updates, not per-level curvature control from prefix-transition scores, not radial position from context entropy, not Gromov-delta or ancestor-depth weighting, not a standalone hyperbolic auxiliary loss. It is the only repulsive, hinge-bounded, margin-terminated operator here, it acts on the QUANTISED code vectors rather than on the input points (so it can split a cluster but not create one), and it is paired with extra deep capacity instead of being asked to fit into the saturated three-level codebook.
ideas.observables: A rise in distinct level-3 prefixes above 2201 and in distinct level-4 prefixes (target well above 3000); a modest rise in mean hyperbolic radius; a fall in mean cosine similarity between quantised vectors of text-kNN pairs; higher L4 codebook perplexity than the level-3 baseline; behaviour-conditioned prefix transition predictability recorded as a diagnostic; and Stage3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 gate, with distinct-prefix counts as the mechanism-level reading.
risks: The outward drift can over-separate and starve the deep codebooks (all items far from every codeword) - the hinge margin limits this but L4 perplexity is the failure meter. The push can destroy text semantics that Stage 3 relies on for cold prefixes, in which case recall falls while prefix counts look healthy. A fourth token lengthens every Stage 3 sequence and may interact badly with the frozen protocol's context. Behaviour-contrast is measured only for items with outgoing transitions, so sparse items contribute nothing and the effect may be unevenly distributed. Seed noise is unmeasured because there is one run.
ideas.safeguards: clamp the artanh argument to 1 - 1e-6 and add 1e-8 in every norm denominator; the exp map keeps |q| < 1 by construction so no ball projection is needed inside the distance; c_ij = 0 for items with no outgoing transition so they contribute no gradient; the hinge is bounded below at 0 with zero gradient once d_P >= m, so the objective has no minimum at the origin and cannot reproduce the round-one collapse (checked explicitly against that failure mode); the level-2 mask is detached so it cannot be gamed by moving an item across parent cells; skip the push for any step whose pair set is empty or whose value is non-finite (logged, never silently zeroed for the whole run); radial rescale at the 0.95 boundary fraction to stop outward drift; dead-code watch on level 4 (perplexity < 2 recorded as a failure signature, not as a gate).
ideas.spec_equations:
c = 1; V = 24556; d = latent/embedding dim; L levels = 4; K = 256.
Precompute (once, CPU/GPU, training split only):
  A[i,j] = #{t : seq_t = i, seq_{t+1} = j, seq in D_train}
  p_i = (A[i,:] + 1) / (A[i,:].sum() + V)
  c_ij = clip(1 - dot(p_i,p_j)/(||p_i|| ||p_j|| + 1e-8), 0, 1)
  NB(i) = 8 nearest items by cosine in frozen text embedding
  P = { (i,j) : j in NB(i), rank by c_ij desc, keep top 4, c_ij >= median_{i,j in NB} c_ij }
Forward:
  u_i = sum_{l=1..4} e_{l, k_l(i)}
  q_i = exp_0^c(u_i) = tanh(||u_i||) * u_i / ||u_i||   (c = 1; u_i = 0 -> 0)
  q_j likewise; b = (-q_i) (+)_1 q_j = ((-q_i) + q_j)/(1 - <q_i,q_j>)   [note (-q_i)(+)q_j uses <q_i,q_j> in the denominator for c = 1]
  d_P(i,j) = 2 * artanh( min(||b||, 1 - 1e-6) )
  push_ij = c_ij * max(0, m - d_P(q_i,q_j))^2
  L_push = mean over batch pairs with pi2(i) == pi2(j) (pi2 detached); if no such pair, L_push = 0
  L = L_RQVAE + lambda * L_push,  lambda = stop_grad(L_quant at step 0) / stop_grad(L_push at step 0)
Backward: STE so dL/du_i flows into e_{1..4, k_l(i)}; k_l(i) from the current hard assignment (no gradient).
Post-step safety: if mean |q| > 0.95, multiply all codebooks by 0.95/mean|q|.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen item text embeddings, training-only transition counts A, the four codebooks e_{l,k} in the tangent at the origin, the batch of item indices with their current hard assignments k_1..k_4. Outputs: the per-step scalar L_push and its gradient into the level-1..4 codebooks, and after training a 4-token SID (k1,k2,k3,k4) per item plus the updated encoder and codebooks.

specification.text: For each item i, q_i = exp_0^c( sum_{l=1..4} e_{l,k_l(i)} ). Static precompute: p_i = add-one-smoothed directed training-transition distribution; contrast c_ij = 1 - cos(p_i,p_j); impostor set P = for each i the 4 text-kNN neighbours (frozen text embedding) with the largest c_ij. Margin m = median over P of d_P at initialisation. Loss L = L_RQVAE + lambda * mean_{(i,j) in batch, pi2(i)=pi2(j)} c_ij * [m - d_P(q_i,q_j)]_+^2, with STE so grad reaches e_{l,k_l(i)}; lambda = L_quant^(0)/L_push^(0) measured at step 0.

ideas.title: Contrast-weighted geodesic repulsion on quantised codewords with a fourth RQ level

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: u_i = 0 for all items, so theta_i = 0 and Rot_i = I; curvature 1, the Lorentz metric and the [256,512,512] capacity are kept; the level-3 partition is the plain shared-codebook partition.
ideas.ablation_both_on: curvature-1 Lorentz assignment plus the successor-contrast holonomy tilt on every item with u_i != 0, capacity [256,512,512], frozen losses and frozen Stage-3 protocol. This is the only arm trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c -> 0, i.e. the standard Euclidean RQ-VAE with the same [256,512,512] capacity, Euclidean assignment and Euclidean residual; the triangle area and hence the tilt vanish identically.
ideas.behavior_computation: Stage-2 TRAIN split only. m_i is the smallest prefix of i's outgoing transitions covering at least 50% of i's total outgoing mass (a derived count, not tuned); Succ(i) = those m_i successors; Control(i) = m_i items drawn deterministically by a hash of (i, m_i) from the pool with train popularity within +-20% of the mean successor popularity and zero transition count from i; u_i = normalize(P(mean_{Succ} t_j - mean_{Control} t_j)), with P the frozen text-to-latent linear map and t_j the frozen text embeddings. Items with no outgoing transitions get u_i = 0. Computed once before Stage 2 and frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Successor-contrast direction per training item: the mean frozen text embedding of its high-mass directed successors minus the mean of popularity-matched non-successors, mapped into the latent tangent at the origin.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute of u_i once (seconds). Per step one O(d) rotation plus one Gram-Schmidt per item: ~1e6 flops per step at 24 steps/epoch and 3000 epochs, under 1% of the measured 0.145-0.16 s/epoch; plus 2 x 256 x d codebook parameters (~16k floats). Estimated 0.15-0.155 s/epoch, inside the four-GPU budget.
ideas.coupling_equation: k*_3(i) = argmin_k d_L( x_i , exp_p( Rot( log_p(e_k) ; theta_i, rho, u_i^perp ) ) ) = argmax_k [ <Rot_i r_i, w_k>_p - ||w_k||_p^2/2 ], the behaviour term supplying u_i^perp and the curved term supplying theta_i and the metric.
ideas.coupling_path: u_i (train-only behaviour) -> rotation plane in T_p -> holonomy angle theta_i from the curvature-1 triangle -> Rot_i applied to r_i -> level-3 code index k* -> 3-token SID -> Stage 3. Setting u_i = 0 makes theta_i = 0 and Rot_i the identity; taking c -> 0 makes the triangle area zero and Rot_i the identity under a Euclidean metric. Only the both-on path changes the deep partition.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the deep fan is tilted toward successor-contrast, the extra 512-codeword level-3 capacity acts as discriminative tokens, distinct L3 prefixes exceed the round-one 2201 and Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065; if the tilt is only assignment noise, prefixes stay flat and recall falls below the frozen baseline.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the level-3 quantization step of Stage-2 training, between the encoder residual and the codebook match; not in the loss, not in the codebook parameterisation, not in Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 on the Lorentz hyperboloid (a gauge fixing, since curvature is a gauge) and the holonomy angle of a geodesic triangle, equal to its hyperbolic area pi/2 - alpha - beta, acting as an SO(2) rotation of T_p.
ideas.key_change: At level 3 only, each item's residual tangent vector is rotated by an angle equal to the hyperbolic area of the triangle (origin, prefix point, unit contrast probe), inside the plane spanned by the radial direction and that item's successor-contrast direction; the rotated query is matched against the ordinary residual codebook, which stays in one canonical frame.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Only train-split transitions, train-split popularity and frozen text embeddings enter u_i; validation and test items, interactions and metrics are never read; every codebook and the SID vocabulary are fitted on train items only, so no validation or test interaction can reach the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: Both negative rounds moved item points toward a behaviour hub, which is algebraically a linear tilt of the assignment target and provably merges prefixes (L3 2201 -> 1298 cost 0.0027 recall). The frozen baseline (~0.0679) keeps a fine deep partition. What is missing is resolution in the direction the behaviour signal actually lives: the deepest level must be re-angled toward each item's successor-contrast direction, because the round-three diagnostics show the radial direction is group compactness, not hierarchy.
ideas.novelty: An ISOMETRY OF THE TANGENT FRAME instead of a movement of points. No radial objective (so the round-one origin collapse is structurally absent), no successor Fréchet codebook, no per-level curvature control, no radial behaviour ranking, no branching MoE. The curved object is the holonomy (geodesic-triangle area) of the Lorentz model used as a rotation angle; the behaviour object is the per-item successor-contrast direction used only as a rotation plane. Capacity is added exactly where the evidence says it was lost: levels 2 and 3 go from 256 to 512 codewords, with the 3-token SID length and the frozen Stage-3 protocol untouched.
ideas.observables: Level-3 indices change for every item with u_i != 0 (expected >90% of items); distinct L3 prefixes and level-3 usage entropy rise above the round-one 2201 (and round-two 1298); mean level-3 residual norm stays above 0.7x the round-one value (mechanism not inert); behaviour-conditioned adjacency and transfer-predictability diagnostics are recorded but not gated; final judgement is Stage-3 test_recall@10 against 0.065.
risks: The reconstruction objective can shrink the level-3 residual until the tilt is inert. Behaviour is item-specific while the codebook is shared, so the codebook cannot rotate for all items and reconstruction loss rises. theta reaching ~45-50 degrees at depth can turn the deepest token into an unusable extra bit. Items with no outgoing transitions get no tilt, splitting the population. Stage 3 may find a behaviour-tilted L3 harder to generate than a reconstruction residual.
ideas.safeguards: theta is in [0, pi/2) by construction and clipped to [0, 1.5]; Rot = I whenever u_i = 0, a_i < 1e-6 or u_perp degenerates, so the fallback is exactly the baseline assignment; a_i and b are clamped to [1e-4, 30] to keep sinh/tanh finite; the frame is detached, so the rotation is a constant isometry that cannot amplify gradients or be cancelled by the encoder learning; no objective term is minimised at the ball's origin, so the round-one collapse mode is structurally absent; distinct L1 prefix count (~250 healthy) and mean level-3 residual norm are monitored as collapse/inertness checks; all diagnostics are recorded, never used as admission gates.
ideas.spec_equations: <x,y>_L = -x0 y0 + x.y, <x,x>_L = -1, o = (1,0,...,0), d_L(x,y) = arccosh(-<x,y>_L). log_p(y) = (d/|y - cosh(d) p|)(y - cosh(d) p); exp_p(v) = cosh(|v|) p + sinh(|v|) v/|v|. Radial unit tangent: rho = sinh(D) o + coth(D)(p - p0 o), D = arccosh(p0). Transport: PT_{o->p}(v) = v + (<p,v>_L/(1 - <o,p>_L))(p + o). v_i = PT(u_i); u_perp = v_i - <v_i,rho>_L rho; if ||u_perp||_L < 1e-8 then Rot = I. a_i = clip(d_L(o,x_i), 1e-4, 30); b = clip(median_i d_L(o,x_i), 1e-4, 30); alpha = atan(tanh(b)/sinh(a_i)); beta = atan(tanh(a_i)/sinh(b)); theta_i = clip(pi/2 - alpha - beta, 0, 1.5). w_par = <w,rho> rho + <w,u_perp> u_perp; Rot(w) = (w - w_par) + cos(theta) w_par + sin(theta)(<w,rho> u_perp - <w,u_perp> rho). q_i = Rot_i^{-1}(r_i) with the frame detached; k* = argmin_k ||q_i - w_k||_p^2; reconstruction point exp_p(Rot_i^{-1}(w_k*)) with the frozen straight-through estimator.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train transition counts, train popularity, frozen text embeddings and map P, the level-2 prefix point p, the encoder point x_i, the 512-entry level-3 codebook, the measured b. Outputs: level-3 code index k* (the third SID token), the rotated reconstruction point for the STE, and per-epoch diagnostics (theta histogram, mean |r_3|, distinct L3 prefix count, level-3 usage entropy).

specification.text: c gauge-fixed to 1. Levels [256,512,512]. Levels 1-2 and all losses are the frozen recipe. Level 3: k* = argmax_k [ <Rot_i r_i, w_k>_p - ||w_k||_p^2/2 ], with r_i = log_p(x_i), w_k = log_p(e_k), p the level-2 prefix point; Rot_i is the SO(2) rotation of angle theta_i = pi/2 - alpha - beta in the orthonormal pair (rho, u_perp), alpha = atan(tanh(b)/sinh(a_i)), beta = atan(tanh(a_i)/sinh(b)), a_i = d_L(o,x_i), b = median_i d_L(o,x_i) measured once after epoch 1 and then frozen. The frame (theta_i, rho, u_perp) is detached from autograd.

ideas.title: Behaviour-contrast holonomy tilt of the deepest residual codebook in a Lorentz RQ-VAE

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: b_i set to the constant 0.5 for every item and the four groups formed by text-only quartiles of the cell's latent along its first principal direction, so no transition statistic enters anchors or weights; the curved operator is kept.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full operator as specified, prototypes from asymmetry quantiles under Poincaré centroids and the assignment using the weighted sum of two Poincaré distances.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c treated as Euclidean, d_c replaced by the Euclidean distance, Fréchet centroids replaced by arithmetic means for both prototypes and assignment; b and the two-anchor weighting are kept.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training sessions only, count F[i,j] = number of times item i is immediately followed by item j. Row-normalise F[i,:] into p_succ(i,·) and column-normalise F[:,i] into p_pred(i,·); b_i = s_i · JSD(p_succ(i,·), p_pred(i,·)) / log 2 in [0,1], with s_i = n_i/(n_i+5) and n_i = sum_j F[i,j] + sum_j F[j,i]; if n_i < 5 then b_i is set to the median of b over items with n_i >= 5 (a documented fallback, not a tuned value). b is computed once before Stage 2 and stored per item.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-transition asymmetry per item, i.e. how different the items that follow an item are from the items that precede it (entry versus terminal character), with support-based shrinkage, restricted to the training split.
ideas.cost_estimate: +1024 trainable and +1024 frozen child vectors (d=64: about 131k parameters, under 1% of the encoder); per step 4096 items x 4 children x 2 anchors = 32768 Poincaré distances at d=64 (about 4M FLOP, under 3% of an encoder step) plus 4096 four-way argmins. At the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs, 0.145-0.16 s/epoch) the projected overhead is at most +0.004 s/epoch, i.e. at most +12 s over the whole Stage-2 run; the one-off quantile/centroid pass is O(N log N) over 24556 items and costs seconds.
ideas.coupling_equation: l4(i) = argmin_{j in {0,1,2,3}} [ d_c(xi_i, u_{k,j}) + b_i · d_c(xi_i, v_{k,j}) ] with k = (l1(i), l2(i), l3(i)) and v_{k,j} = Fréchet_c({xi : item in asymmetry quantile j of cell k}).
ideas.coupling_path: b_i gives the asymmetry quantile groups of the level-3 cell; those define the frozen hyperbolic centroids v_kj and also supply the per-item weight; both enter the two-anchor Poincaré score; the argmin emits l4; the SID becomes the Stage-3 token. Removing the behaviour term changes both the anchors' ordering and the weight, hence l4; removing the curved operation changes the centroid construction and both distances, hence l4.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping only if the fourth digit actually spreads items, i.e. distinct four-token SIDs rise from about 2201 to at least 6000 with no level-3 cell collapsing onto a single child, and child index tracks the asymmetry quantile the child was born from. If both hold, Stage 3 sees a finer, behaviour-labelled deep partition without any input displacement and test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065. If the digit collapses (all items of a cell to one child) the mechanism is a no-op and the merge lesson predicts no gain.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Only in the level-4 (deepest) quantizer: it builds the frozen child prototypes from the asymmetry quantiles and supplies both distance terms of the assignment; levels 1-3 keep the frozen Euclidean RQ path and the decoder keeps its Euclidean reconstruction, so curved and Euclidean pieces meet inside one operator.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincaré ball of curvature -c with c = (1/(1.2R))^2 derived from the measured initial latent radius R; Möbius addition (+); Poincaré distance d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)·||(-x)(+)y||); and the hyperbolic Fréchet centroid via a fixed-point log/exp mean.
ideas.key_change: Add a fourth SID token from a shared alphabet {0,1,2,3}, keyed by (l1,l2,l3,child); child vectors are trainable but born at frozen hyperbolic asymmetry-quantile centroids, and each assignment is the argmin over j of d_c(xi,u_kj) + b_i·d_c(xi,v_kj).
ideas.leakage_boundary: F, b, the quantile groups and the frozen prototypes v are computed exclusively from training sequences and training-item latents; validation and test sequences are read only by the frozen Stage-3 protocol. Prototypes are frozen at the end of epoch 1 from training items only, and the SID table is built from training items only; validation/test items are encoded by the frozen Stage-2 encoder and given digits by the same argmin rule using only frozen prototypes and frozen b, so no validation or test interaction can enter the SID construction. No test statistic chooses c, the smoothing prior, or the number of children.
ideas.motivation: The frozen chain is depth-starved: 24556 items share only 2201 distinct level-3 triples (about 1.24 level-3 codes per level-2 cell), so the deepest frozen level is nearly redundant, and every mechanism tried so far reduced that count further (1298 in round two) and lost recall. Behaviour information that separates items by how they are consumed predicts recall, but round two injected it by displacing item points toward a behaviour hub, which merged prefixes. The problem: put behaviour into the deepest tokens while increasing, not decreasing, the number of distinct deep cells.
ideas.novelty: No global codebook is re-weighted, no input point is moved, no successor barycentre, no entropy/radial ranking, no per-level curvature scalar. A hierarchical product digit is attached per level-3 cell: each cell owns four child prototypes that are hyperbolic Fréchet centroids of the cell's directed-transition ASYMMETRY quantiles (forward-successor distribution versus backward-predecessor distribution), and the child is chosen by a two-anchor weighted Poincaré score whose second term is scaled by the item's own asymmetry. None of per-cell shared-alphabet refinement, forward/backward asymmetry, or a two-anchor weighted Poincaré assignment exists in the repository, and the two-term sum is precisely what keeps the curvature from being a pure gauge.
ideas.observables: distinct four-token SID count and per-cell child entropy (expect at least 6000 distinct and non-degenerate mass); correlation between child index and the asymmetry quantile the child was born from; prefix-conditioned next-token accuracy at position 4 versus positions 1-3; level-4 token usage in the Stage-3 generator; final Stage-3 test_recall@10 against 0.065 and against the 0.05439 and 0.05165 references.
risks: (1) A fourth token lengthens Stage-3 generation by one step and may cost precision even with a finer SID. (2) Transition asymmetry may be sparse: items with fewer than 5 transitions fall back to the smoothed default and their children degrade toward text quartiles, so behaviour stops reaching the tokens. (3) Freezing v at the end of epoch 1 may lock a bad geometry if the encoder drifts; an EMA would introduce a non-derivable constant, so it is deliberately not used. (4) Curvature is a gauge, so any measured gain must come from the two-anchor sum and the per-cell prototypes, not from the value of c. (5) Child usage imbalance could make the 4-symbol alphabet effectively binary.
ideas.safeguards: clamp sqrt(c)||x|| to <= 1-1e-5 before every artanh and clamp the artanh argument to <= 1-1e-6; replace any non-finite b_i or centroid with the cell mean; cells with fewer than 8 items use four replicated children and no reseed; the dead-child reseed prevents alphabet collapse to one symbol; the epoch-1 freeze and the reseed epochs are the only schedule constants and are fixed fractions of the 3000-epoch budget, with no value chosen by trying alternatives; per-cell child entropy is logged every 100 epochs so the round-one collapse failure mode is visible rather than silent.
ideas.spec_equations: (1) F, p_succ, p_pred as above with +1e-9 smoothing; b_i = s_i·JSD(p_succ(i,·),p_pred(i,·))/log 2; s_i = n_i/(n_i+5). (2) c = (1/(1.2R))^2 with R = max over the 24556 initial training latents of ||xi||. (3) End of epoch 1, for each level-3 cell k: sort S_k by b ascending (ties by item id), cut into four equal-mass groups Q_k0..Q_k3 (if |S_k| < 8 replicate one group four times); v_kj = Fréchet_c(Q_kj) by m = mean(Q_kj), then 5 times m = exp_m(mean_{x in Q_kj} log_m(x)), and if sqrt(c)||m|| > 0.95 then m = m·0.95/(sqrt(c)||m||); set u_kj = v_kj. (4) Every step: compute l1,l2,l3 with the frozen RQ path; r4 = xi - (c_l1+c_l2+c_l3); score_j = d_c(r4, u_kj) + b_i·d_c(r4, v_kj); l4 = argmin_j; q = c_l1+c_l2+c_l3+u_k[l4]+sg(r4-u_k[l4]); loss = ||dec(q)-dec_target||^2 + ||sg(q)-xi||^2 + beta·||q-sg(xi)||^2 with beta as in the frozen recipe, u_k[l4] updated by the gradient through q. (5) Deterministic dead-child reseed at the ends of epochs 10, 30, 100 and 300 (fixed fractions of the 3000-epoch budget): any child whose EMA mass in its cell is below 0.02 is moved to the cell item farthest in d_c from the cell's assigned set; the EMA is 1/(1+t) so no decay constant is chosen.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the current RQ latent xi (dim d), its level-1..3 codes, the frozen per-item scalar b_i in [0,1], the frozen prototype table v (256 cells x 4 x d) and the trainable child table u (same shape). Output is the integer l4 in {0,1,2,3} plus the quantized vector q in R^d; the index is stop-gradient and only the chosen child vector is differentiable.

specification.text: Offline on the training split, build the first-order transition count matrix F and the per-item support-shrunk forward/backward Jensen-Shannon asymmetry b_i in [0,1]. Fix c = (1/(1.2R))^2 from the measured initial latent radius R. At the end of epoch 1, cut every level-3 cell's items into four equal-mass b-quantiles, compute each quantile's hyperbolic Fréchet centroid v_kj, and clone it into a trainable u_kj. Every step the frozen levels 1-3 run unchanged; level 4 is the argmin of the two-anchor score; the quantized latent is q1+q2+q3+u_k[l4] with a straight-through residual; the baseline reconstruction and commitment losses now include level 4.

ideas.title: Directed-transition asymmetry carved into a per-cell 4-symbol fourth SID digit by hyperbolic quantile bisection

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: identical code path with the contrast switch set so btilde_i = 0 for all items; then u_k = 0, rho_k = 0, both children equal c_k, the argmin ties resolve to '+' and the level-L alphabet is effectively K, i.e. the plain baseline quantizer at that depth.
ideas.ablation_both_on: full mechanism, fixed c = 1 Poincare exp/log/distance with the contrast-derived children; this is the single trained arm.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: identical code path with Euclidean replacements exp(v) = c + v, log(z) = z - c, d = d_E; children sit at c_k ± rho_k u_k and both anchor and child selection are Euclidean nearest neighbour, with all behaviour statistics unchanged.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 TRAINING split only: A_ij = number of times item j occurs immediately after item i in a training sequence (window 1). Row-normalize to p_out(i), column-normalize to p_in(i), b_i = p_out(i) - p_in(i) (sparse, length |I|). Project once with a fixed Gaussian matrix G in R^{D x |I|}, G_ab ~ N(0,1/D), seeded by the recipe's data seed: btilde_i = G b_i, set to 0 if ||btilde_i|| < 1e-8. Computed before Stage 2 starts and frozen for the whole run.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-transition contrast per item: the difference between the item's successor distribution and its predecessor distribution, i.e. how much it is a "source" vs a "sink" in the training transition graph.
ideas.cost_estimate: +K extra level-L codeword embeddings in Stage 2 (K*D parameters, e.g. 256*64 = 16k) and +K extra SID token rows in the Stage-3 embedding table. Per step at frozen scale: batch ~1023 items (24556 items / 24 steps), one log map and 2K-way distance evaluation at level L, ~2*1023*2K*D ~ 1.3e8 FLOPs, i.e. well under 1% of the encoder/decoder pass. One-time precompute of btilde over 24556 items is O(nnz(transitions)*D). Expected Stage-2 epoch time 0.150-0.163 s on four GPUs, inside the measured budget.
ideas.coupling_equation: token_i = 2 * argmin_k d_c(p_i, c_k) + [ argmin_{pi in {+,-}} d_c(p_i, exp_{c_{a_i}}(pi * rho_{a_i} * u_{a_i})) ], with u_{a} = normalize(EMA[ mean_{i in A_a} btilde_i ]) and rho_a = EMA[ median_{i in A_a} |<log_{c_a}(p_i), u_a>| ]; the behaviour term is btilde_i inside u_a and rho_a, the curved term is d_c and exp_{c_a}.
ideas.coupling_path: train-only transition contrast btilde -> per-anchor EMA mean direction u_k and EMA median tangent extent rho_k -> child codeword positions exp_{c_k}(±rho_k u_k) in the ball -> Poincare nearest child -> level-L SID token -> Stage-3 token sequence. Behaviour alone without the curved exp/log would give a flat Euclidean offset with no anchor-local frame; geometry alone without behaviour gives u_k = 0 and rho_k = 0, so the two children coincide and the computation collapses exactly to the K-codeword baseline. Removing either changes the emitted tokens.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If deep-prefix merging is what cost rounds one and two, and if behaviour contrast is the discriminative behaviour signal, then this mechanism should raise distinct L3 token usage from ~K to >1.5K, leave the L1/L2 prefix counts at the baseline level (~251/1769), and push Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 (target: at or above the 0.0679 frozen baseline) in one run. Worth keeping if L3 distinct tokens rise materially while L1/L2 stay flat and recall does not regress; the decisive observation is test_recall@10 > 0.065 with recall@5 and ndcg@10 moving consistently.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer's deepest assignment step (curved quantization): it decides both the anchor (Poincare nearest neighbour) and the child codeword position (Poincare exponential map from the anchor), and thus the level-L SID token emitted to Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (gauge-fixed, since scaling the tangent by 1/sqrt(c) reproduces c=1 exactly): Poincare distance d_c, exponential map exp_{c_k} on the tangent space at an anchor, and logarithmic map log_{c_k} used to measure the contrast projection. Applied at the deepest quantizer level only.
ideas.key_change: Replace the deepest level's K-codeword nearest-neighbour by a 2K structured codebook: each anchor codeword c_k spawns two children exp_{c_k}(±rho_k u_k), where u_k is the EMA of the mean behaviour-contrast vector of the items currently assigned to anchor k and rho_k is the EMA of the median absolute tangent projection of those items on u_k. Anchor selection and child selection are both hyperbolic nearest-neighbour, so the level-3 token is a function of the behaviour-derived child placements.
ideas.leakage_boundary: btilde uses only training-split sequences and is frozen before any Stage-2 step; no validation or test sequence is read. beta, the curvature (=1), the projection seed and the 0.5 spacing factor are fixed a priori; the only data-dependent constant, the spacing bound, is measured from the current train-fitted codebook, never from validation recall. Stage 3 receives only the frozen SID file and never re-reads behaviour. No hyperparameter is selected by validation.
ideas.motivation: The two negative rounds both lost recall exactly when deep prefix capacity fell (2201 distinct L3 prefixes → 0.0544; 1298 → 0.0517), and both lost capacity by moving input points toward a behaviour hub. The behaviour signal that does predict recall on the 107 confirmed pairs is behaviour-CONTRAST, not Gromov-delta, not ancestor depth. So the useful place for behaviour is not the item position (it merges) but the DEEP CODEBOOK: let the deepest level be doubled into behaviour-polarized child codewords whose offsets are measured from the training transition contrast, so the level-3 partition becomes strictly finer and the extra tokens carry behaviour rather than duplicating it.
ideas.novelty: Round one/two moved items and residuals (merging). The rejected ideas ranked items radially (BRad-RQ), set curvature from a prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), used successor-weighted Fréchet codebook means (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), or built cones/tree-embeddings. None of them *generated extra codewords* from a behaviour statistic. Here no point moves; the codebook itself is refined by a measured behaviour contrast through the Poincaré exponential map, doubling deep-level capacity at zero free parameters (the offsets are buffers, not trained), so it cannot collapse to the origin and cannot over-merge.
ideas.observables: number of distinct level-L tokens actually used (expect ~K -> >1.5K), L1/L2 prefix counts (expect ~unchanged at ~251/~1769), per-anchor child-usage entropy and fraction of anchors with both children used, Stage-2 reconstruction curve, then Stage-3 test_recall@10, recall@5, ndcg@10, plus the recorded behaviour diagnostics (consecutive-SID transition adjacency and prefix transfer predictability).
risks: Contrast may be zero or near-zero for many items (isolated, cold, or symmetric items), leaving one child per anchor unused and the gain near zero. The fixed random projection of the contrast may be misaligned with the directions the encoder actually uses. Placing children off the anchor raises the level-L reconstruction error if the argmin does not compensate. Since levels 1..L-1 are untouched, if the true bottleneck is L1/L2 granularity the gain is capped. A moving codebook during the 3000-epoch schedule can chase the EMA; a one-epoch window mitigates but may oscillate. Anchors near the ball boundary get strongly curved children.
ideas.safeguards: fix c = 1 (gauge) so no curvature tuning exists; clip ||p|| to 1-1e-5 and the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-12 before every d_c/log_c; Möbius addition keeps exp_c inside the ball by construction, and rho_k is additionally capped at half the measured median nearest-anchor spacing so children cannot cross into a neighbouring cell; if any buffer is non-finite keep its previous value; anchors with m_k = 0 keep their buffers and emit only their '+' child so the alphabet never breaks; sign(0) resolves to '+'; buffers are stop-gradient so no new gradient path can destabilise the encoder; the new token ids are appended to both the Stage-2 codebook table and the Stage-3 SID vocabulary with a fixed offset.
ideas.spec_equations:
exp_0(r) = tanh(||r||/2) * r/||r||, exp_c(v) = c (+) tanh(||v||/2) * v/||v||
  d_c(p,q) = arcosh(1 + 2||p-q||^2 / ((1-||p||^2)(1-||q||^2)))
  log_c(z) = 2 * artanh(||(-c) (+) z||) * ((-c) (+) z)/||(-c) (+) z||
  step(t):
    z <- Encoder(x) ; (levels 1..L-1 quantized as baseline) ; r <- residual
    p <- exp_0(r) ; a <- argmin_k d_c(p, c_k)
    pi <- argmin_{+-} d_c(p, exp_{c_a}(+- rho_a u_a)) ; j <- 2a + (pi+1)/2
    zhat <- Decoder(quantized(z, j)) ; loss <- baseline reconstruction loss (unchanged)
  after optimizer step:
    for each k with m_k = |A_k| > 0:
      s <- mean_{i in A_k} btilde_i ; u_k <- normalize((1-beta)u_k + beta s)
      r <- median_{i in A_k} |<log_{c_k}(p_i), u_k>| ; rho_k <- (1-beta)rho_k + beta r
    dn <- median_k min_{k'!=k} d_c(c_k, c_k') ; rho_k <- min(rho_k, 0.5*dn)
  beta = 1/24, c = 1, u_k(0) = 0, rho_k(0) = 0
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: per-item deepest-level residual r_i (or encoder latent), anchor codebook {c_k} from the baseline recipe, per-item frozen contrast btilde_i, buffers u_k and rho_k, curvature c = 1, beta = 1/24. Outputs: level-L token index j_i in [0, 2K), quantized vector exp_{c_{a_i}}(pi_i rho_{a_i} u_{a_i}), and updated buffers; the SID becomes (level 1..L-1 tokens, j_i).

specification.text:
Fix c=1 (curvature is a gauge; fixing it costs no generality). Levels 1..L-1 are untouched. For level L with anchor codebook {c_k} in the Poincare ball:
  p_i = exp_0(r_i) ; a_i = argmin_k d_c(p_i, c_k)
  u_k <- normalize( (1-beta) u_k + beta * (1/m_k) * sum_{i in A_k} btilde_i )
  rho_k <- (1-beta) rho_k + beta * median_{i in A_k} |<log_{c_k}(p_i), u_k>|
  c_{k,+} = exp_{c_k}(+rho_k u_k), c_{k,-} = exp_{c_k}(-rho_k u_k)
  pi_i = argmin_{pi in {+,-}} d_c(p_i, c_{a_i,pi}) ; token_i = 2*a_i + (pi_i+1)/2
with beta = 1/24 (one-epoch window, derived from 24 steps/epoch), u_k, rho_k stop-gradient EMA buffers, updated after each optimizer step. btilde_i is the fixed-seed projected contrast from the train split only. rho_k is capped at 0.5 * median_k min_{k'!=k} d_c(c_k, c_k') (measured codebook spacing; the pair may not overlap a neighbouring Voronoi cell).

ideas.title: Behaviour-contrast hyperbolic dyadic refinement of the deepest RQ codebook

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: code path BEH_DIR=0: h_i forced to 0 and g_i forced to 1, so u_i = vhat_i and the fourth level is the plain curvature-normalised geodesic step off the level-3 prefix. Token stream, loss and every other hyperparameter identical. Not trained this round; wired and unit-tested.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full specified run: BEH_DIR=1 and GEO=1, behaviour direction and gates live, log/exp/lambda/d_P live, K4=64, s0 measured once at epoch 0, W initialised to 0, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, then the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol. The only arm trained.

ideas.key_change: After the third RQ level each item is moved a fixed, learnable geodesic distance s away from its level-3 prefix point along a direction that mixes (a) the Poincare log of its level-3 text residual, metric-normalised by the prefix conformal factor, with (b) a fixed orthonormal projection of its training-only successor profile; the nearest of 64 ball-embedded codewords to the arrival point becomes its fourth SID token.
ideas.leakage_boundary: T is built only from train-split sessions; validation and test sequences are never read, counted, or used to fit the SVD, P, s0 or the epoch-0 k-means. ideas.motivation: Both trained rounds lost recall for one reason - their mechanisms edited the existing three-level partition and merged prefixes (2201 -> 1298 distinct L3 prefixes traced the 0.0544 -> 0.0517 drop). This mechanism attacks the one place where room demonstrably exists - an ADDITIONAL level - and uses training-only successor behaviour to choose the direction of that refinement, so items a user will treat differently stop sharing a SID while the surviving 2201-prefix capacity is provably untouched.
ideas.novelty: Every mechanism here so far (round-one curved residual chain, round-two concentration-scaled step to the popularity-adjusted successor barycentre, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, succboost-geoshift, BRad-RQ radial entropy assignment, CURVCTRL-SID, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, TSG-SID, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, SUCC-GEO-CBTAB, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS) re-positions points or codewords of the EXISTING partition, i.e. it spends existing capacity. This idea is additive: levels 1-3 are frozen bit-identical, and behaviour is neither a hub attraction nor a radius rescaling in the existing ball - it is a DIRECTION for a new fourth token. There is no Frechet/successor barycentre anywhere (behaviour enters as a rank-32 SVD coordinate of the item's own successor distribution, not as an averaged successor position) and no entropy-driven radial scaling (no item's radius is changed).
ideas.observables: (a) distinct L4 token count and distinct four-token SID count versus 2201 L3 prefixes (should rise; 251/1769/2201 should not move); (b) share of the level-4 reconstruction term in total reconstruction error (should stay non-trivial, i.e. level 4 still carries text geometry); (c) MI between an item's a4 and the a4 of its next training item versus MI against random items (deep token behaviour-informative); (d) measured s and |W| trajectories (s away from clamps, W unsaturated); (e) Stage-3 test_recall@10, recall@5, ndcg@10.
risks: (i) the behaviour term dominates u_i so level four degenerates into a 64-way behaviour-cluster id shared across prefixes and text residual is lost - visible as near-uniform a4 across prefixes and a small level-4 reconstruction share; (ii) learnable s hits the lower clamp, level four becomes a no-op (bounded, not destructive); (iii) fixed random P lands the successor profile in directions already dominant in the text residual, so the mix adds nothing; (iv) Stage-3 pays one extra sequence position at the same epoch budget.
ideas.safeguards: (1) every ball point is clamp-projected to radius <= 1-1e-5 before any log map; (2) arcosh/artanh arguments clamped to [1+1e-9, 1-1e-7] so no NaN at coincident or boundary points; (3) |v_i| < 1e-8 falls back to vhat_i = 0 so the direction is behaviour-only rather than undefined; (4) s clamped to [0.37 s0, 2.72 s0] so the fourth level can neither vanish nor jump to the boundary, with s0 measured at epoch 0 so no scale is hand-chosen; (5) the gate is 1+tanh, bounded in (0,2), so it can never zero the residual; (6) no objective term has its minimum at the ball origin - q_i sits at geodesic distance s from p_i and s is clamped away from 0 - so the round-one origin-collapse failure mode is structurally excluded, and s and |W| are logged every epoch anyway; (7) level-4 codebook usage is logged per epoch (distinct a4 per prefix and globally) so dead-codebook failure is visible in-run; (8) W and psi use the baseline optimiser and learning rate, no new hyperparameter; (9) the level-4 commitment coefficient equals the levels 1-3 coefficient so no weight is introduced; (10) the behaviour profile is precomputed and cached, and zero-transition items deterministically reduce to the behaviour-off path.

objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

Round three. One mechanism along the chain: user behaviour data -> behaviour graph -> tree-structure check -> behaviour item embedding -> Gromov delta -> hyperbolic curvature -> text embedding into a hyperbolic RQ-VAE -> behaviour supervision -> SID -> Stage3 -> test_recall@10. Target: a real test_recall@10 above 0.065 from one frozen four-GPU Stage2 run and one frozen Stage3 run. The baseline is the round-two mechanism tree TIGER_CONCMID-GEO-SID.

WHAT ROUNDS ONE AND TWO MEASURED (all with the frozen chain: Stage2 3000 epochs at 0.145-0.16 s per epoch, Stage3 150 epochs, full protocol):
Round one, a curved residual chain on the frozen text geometry: L1/L2/L3 prefixes 251/1769/2201, test_recall@10 = 0.05439, recall@5 = 0.0360, ndcg@10 = 0.0296.
Round two, a concentration-scaled geodesic step moving each item toward its popularity-adjusted successor barycentre (99.1% of the items moved, median displacement 0.0207): prefixes 230/1251/1298, test_recall@10 = 0.05165, recall@5 = 0.0350, ndcg@10 = 0.0283.
The gate is 0.065; the frozen baseline's own number is about 0.0679. Both mechanisms are NEGATIVE results and both must be treated as such.

THE ONE CONSISTENT SIGNAL ACROSS THE TWO ROUNDS: the deeper prefix capacity is what separates them. Round one kept 2201 distinct L3 prefixes and scored 0.0544; round two kept 1298 and scored 0.0517. Every mechanism that MERGES prefixes has lost recall so far, and every mechanism tried so far has merged them: moving the input points toward a behaviour hub (round two) and a 3-level 256-codeword quantizer whose level three is already saturated. A mechanism that wants to move the number has to make the partition FINER at depth, or use the behaviour signal where it does not cost capacity.

CONSTRAINTS THE PROPOSALS MUST RESPECT: (a) the interaction graph is tree-like but a degree-preserving rewiring is exactly as tree-like, so 'the data is a tree' is unavailable; (b) curvature is a gauge (scaling the tangent by 1/sqrt(c) reproduces curvature 1 exactly), and on the 107 confirmed SID/recall pairs the behaviour-CONTRAST metrics predict recall (+0.7104 plain, +0.7170 Euclidean control, +0.6593 unweighted four-point) while Gromov-delta weighting and ancestor-depth weighting HURT by 0.12 and 0.075, and the radial term is group compactness rather than hierarchy; (c) any mechanism whose objective has its minimum at the ball's origin collapses the encoder (round one did exactly that twice, degenerating to one or two prefixes per level) and must be checked against that failure mode; (d) the behaviour signal must reach the TOKENS, not only the codebook positions.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: one formal training run per candidate (3000 epochs, four-GPU DDP, global batch 4096), no ablation arms, no hyperparameter tuning, no seed sweeps; every constant derivable a priori. The behaviour-off / geometry-off / both-on switches must exist in the code and be wired correctly, but only the both-on arm is trained. Stage3 keeps its frozen protocol. Stage2->Stage3 admission is technical validity only; test_recall@10 > 0.065 is the final judgement, and a negative result must be recorded with its numbers.

papers.title: HVQ-VAE: Variational auto-encoder with hyperbolic vector quantization

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability.
